In the 21st century, leaders are facing new situations that are characterized by volatility, uncertainty, complexity and ambiguity. And top companies identify capacities in leadership that are no critical.

The Master of Arts in Global Leadership can help students develop their skills to tackle complex issues through collaboration, empathy, adaptability, community engagement and systems thinking.

Students will develop the capacity to lead themselves and others through an understanding of complex global systems. Students will be positioned for a market that requires global leadership capacity in a broad range of sectors

Students can customize their learning with courses taught by experts in areas, such as conflict resolution, strategic planning, artificial intelligence, governance, community development, geopolitics, international politics, global civil society and gender.

Program outcomes

Once students have completed their program, students will have to be able to apply practical tools and strategies to address current issues, challenges and opportunities related to global leadership. Students' work will impact the wellbeing of communities and the planet.

In addition, students will be able to do the following:

  • use tools they learn to improve their career versatility, resiliency and adaptability
  • apply sought after soft skills needed in the age of artificial intelligence
  • work with cross-cultural awareness in increasingly culturally-diverse environments
  • work effectively across teams
  • understand systems thinking and approaches important for 21st century complex challenges
  • lead change with knowledge of global socio-political and economic systems drivers.

The MA in Conflict Analysis and Management is a two-year, interdisciplinary graduate program. Students will examine the full spectrum of conflict, from interpersonal to international. Students will gain a holistic, systemic, cross-cultural approach to understand and manage it.

Royal Roads University helps students create self-awareness of their own role in conflict, and how they can make a difference. Students will examine contemporary and innovative research. Students will apply that research to build skills in facilitation, negotiation and mediation. In learning to appreciate their strengths and limitations, students will become a reflective practitioner in the expanding field of conflict management.

The Master of Arts in Environment and Management combines leading-edge research with on-the-ground practice and theory. Students will enhance their existing skills, while increasing your knowledge about how to solve the world's complex environmental challenges.

Students will examine many topics related to sustainability, from climate pollution and biodiversity loss, to reconciliation and social and community innovations. They will also focus on sustainability, accelerating the take-up of social and community innovations and the nature of change. Students will learn about strategic decision making and teamwork. And they will learn how to address technical and policy questions using systems and sustainability perspectives.

By studying the inter-relationships between human, social and ecological systems, and learning about critical management concepts, students will be ready to lead sustainability initiatives in multiple sectors, from government to industry and more.
636c:
Designed with the earth in mind, the Master of Arts in Environmental Education and Communication features a comprehensive curriculum that concerns itself with both the beauty and the despair of the world.

Students in the program will integrate what they know with what they learn , for practical action in their life and work. Students will develop a broader understanding of sustainability, learn general systems theory and cultivate their own ecological identity. In the larger context of learning, RRU students often get outside — of the classroom, and of their own mindsets.

Students will also learn creative and strategic communication skills, and practice design thinking. Worldviews, ecopsychology and Indigenous ways of being and knowing will shape a critical awareness of multiple perspectives, and foster a closer connection with the natural world.

Student learning will focus on how we live, act, relate, teach and communicate. Students will discover more about the interconnectedness of the biosphere through hands-on experience at field school within various Indigenous communities.

This is an invitation to students to build upon their skills and imagination as an environmental educator and communicator. Applied projects and research that makes a difference will let students immediately practice and live what they are learning.

This globalized world — and the cultures and subcultures within it — have specific communication needs.

In the Master of Arts in Intercultural and International Communication program, students will develop the communication skills to bridge relationships in this media-rich, global community.

Informed by theory and practice, students will learn to engage with multiple channels for communication like media, social marketing, advocacy and public culture.

Students will take a strategic approach to media and public relations, applying their knowledge and writing skill to different fields: sport, health, diplomacy and social development.

Students will become familiar with different organizational structures — government, NGO, corporation and not-for-profit — and students will learn ways to engage their audiences.

Graduates of the MA in Intercultural and International Communication will see how communication influences culture, and how culture shapes communities.

Students in the MBA in Executive Management at Royal Roads University can deepen their strategic knowledge of business practices to broaden their influence in the workplace. They can build leadership, analytical and management skills.

The MBA in Executive Management at Royal Roads University gives students the professional advantage to move their career forward.
